customerJourneyStories.name: Adopting one learning portfolio across business units
customerJourneyStories.summary: Adopting one learning portfolio across business units through a bounded pilot and accountable ongoing use.

stages.narrative: Fragmented learning portals and an unproven reskilling program trigger a search for a more accountable learning offer.
The director hears about Studytube through an L&D peer or industry event and explores its product and customer examples.
They compare Studytube with a suite LMS and a content subscription, then review role coverage, migration effort, pricing and data terms with IT and procurement.
They pilot Studytube with one role family, a fixed learning budget and agreed assessment criteria.
The director adopts Studytube for quarterly portfolio reviews once managers and administrators can act on the same evidence.
They renew or expand only if the academy improves relevant development and keeps administration manageable; weak programs are changed before further rollout.

customerJourneyStories.name: Choosing to use the employer academy
customerJourneyStories.summary: Choosing to use the employer academy through a bounded pilot and accountable ongoing use.

stages.narrative: A new assignment or development conversation reveals a learning need the employee cannot easily address through current resources.
The employee hears about the Studytube-powered employer academy from their manager, onboarding communication or a colleague.
Before participating they check relevance, accessibility, time commitment, visibility of their data and whether the employer will support learning during work.
They try one short learning path or a first training booking and check that progress is recorded accurately.
They return to the academy for agreed goals and required learning when the experience consistently fits their work.
They continue using it when managers recognize demonstrated progress and issues with access, records or relevance receive a fair response.
